questions.question: What is the projected fiscal deficit for FY2025-26 as per the Union Budget 2025-26?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4.4% of GDP**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Union Budget 2025-26** was presented by the **Union Minister of Finance**, **Nirmala Sitharaman**, in the **Parliament** of India.
 
• For the **Financial Year 2025-26**, the government has projected the **fiscal deficit** at **4.4%** of the **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**.
 
• This target is part of a broad **fiscal consolidation** roadmap aimed at bringing the deficit down to a sustainable level below **4.5%** of **GDP**.
 
• In the previous fiscal year, **FY 2024-25**, the **Revised Estimate (RE)** for the fiscal deficit was recorded at **4.9%**, demonstrating a steady downward trend from the **Budget Estimate (BE)** of **5.1%**.
 
• The reduction to **4.4%** reflects the government's commitment to balancing **macroeconomic stability** with the need for high **capital expenditure** to spur **economic growth**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fiscal Deficit**: This is the difference between the government's **total expenditure** and its **total non-debt receipts** (which include **revenue receipts** and **non-debt capital receipts** like recovery of loans). It indicates the total **borrowing requirements** of the **Government of India**.
 
• **Revenue Deficit**: This occurs when the **revenue expenditure** exceeds the **revenue receipts**. It implies that the government is borrowing to meet its **current consumption** needs rather than for **investment** or **asset creation**.
 
• **Primary Deficit**: This is calculated by deducting **interest payments** on previous debts from the **fiscal deficit**. It shows the amount of borrowing needed to meet expenditures other than interest obligations.
 
• **FRBM Act, 2003**: The **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act** was introduced to ensure long-term **macroeconomic stability** by setting targets for the reduction of **fiscal** and **revenue deficits**.
 
• **Financing the Deficit**: The government typically finances the **fiscal deficit** through **market borrowings** (issuing **dated securities** and **treasury bills**), **external debt**, and drawing from **small savings funds**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Union Budget 2025-26** continues to prioritize **Capital Expenditure (Capex)**, which is vital for building **infrastructure** such as **highways**, **railways**, and **digital networks**.
 
• A lower **fiscal deficit** helps in keeping **inflation** under control and prevents the "crowding out" effect, ensuring that more **credit** is available for the **private sector**.
 
• The **Tax-to-GDP ratio** is expected to improve in **2025-26** due to better **GST** compliance and a wider **direct tax** base, contributing to the **consolidation** process.
 
• The government intends to stick to the **fiscal glide path** to eventually reduce the **debt-to-GDP ratio**, which is a key metric for **international credit rating agencies**.
</ul

questions.question: Which senior Indian official attended the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Defence Ministers' Conclave in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajnath Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rajnath Singh**, the Union **Minister of Defence** of **India**, attended the **Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Defence Ministers' Conclave** held in **June 2025**.
 
• As the **Defence Minister**, he has been a consistent representative for **India** at high-level security dialogues, focusing on **regional stability** and **military cooperation** across the **Eurasian** landmass.
 
• During the conclave, the **Indian** delegation emphasized the importance of a **multipolar world** and the need for **collective action** against **transborder terrorism**.
 
• The meeting provided a platform for **India** to engage in bilateral discussions with other member states, including **Russia** and **Central Asian Republics**, to strengthen **strategic partnerships**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Rajnath Singh is correct.***
 
• The **Defence Ministers' Conclave** is an annual event where the heads of defense departments from **SCO** member nations deliberate on **defense industry** collaboration and **joint military exercises**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO):**
 
 
• The **SCO** is a permanent **intergovernmental international organization** established on **15 June 2001** in **Shanghai**, **China**.
 
• It was founded by the leaders of **China**, **Kazakhstan**, **Kyrgyzstan**, **Russia**, **Tajikistan**, and **Uzbekistan**.
 
• **India** and **Pakistan** officially joined as full members during the **Astana Summit** in **June 2017**.
 
• In **July 2023**, **Iran** was formally inducted as the **ninth permanent member** of the **SCO**.
 
 
 
• **Structure and Objectives:**
 
 
• The **Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS)**, headquartered in **Tashkent**, is a permanent organ of the **SCO** which facilitates cooperation against **terrorism**, **separatism**, and **extremism**.
 
• The organization covers approximately **40%** of the **global population** and nearly **20%** of the **global GDP**.
 
• The primary goals include strengthening **mutual trust** and **neighborliness** among member states and promoting effective cooperation in **politics**, **trade**, **economy**, and **technology**.
 
 
 
• **India's Role in SCO:**
 
 
• **India** hosted the **SCO Council of Heads of State** summit for the first time in **virtual mode** in **July 2023** under the theme **"SECURE-SCO"**.
 
• The acronym **SECURE** stands for **Security**, **Economy**, **Connectivity**, **Unity**, **Respect**, and **Environment**, a concept proposed by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**.
 
• **India's** engagement with the **SCO** is driven by its **"Connect Central Asia"** policy and its interest in the **International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Regional Security Dynamics:** The **SCO** is often viewed as an **"Alliance of the East"** and plays a critical role in balancing **Western** influence in **Central Asia**.
 
• **Military Exercises:** Member states regularly participate in **"Peace Mission"** joint military counter-terrorism exercises to improve **interoperability** among their armed forces.
 
• **Expansion:** Recent years have seen **Belarus** moving towards full membership, indicating the growing **geopolitical footprint** of the organization in **Eastern Europe** and **Asia**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following veteran Indian goalkeepers announced that he will retire after the Paris Olympics, ending an 18-year career during which he played a pivotal role in some of the team's historic moments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**P R Sreejesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **P R Sreejesh**, the legendary Indian hockey goalkeeper, announced his retirement from international hockey, concluding an illustrious **18-year career** after the **Paris 2024 Olympics**.
 
• He made his senior international debut in **2006** at the **South Asian Games** in **Colombo** and became a permanent fixture in the Indian squad since **2011**.
 
• Sreejesh played a pivotal role in India winning two consecutive Olympic **Bronze medals** at **Tokyo 2020** and **Paris 2024**, ending a long medal drought for the country in hockey.
 
• Over his career, he represented **India** in over **330 international matches** and participated in **four Olympic Games** (**2012, 2016, 2020, and 2024**).
 
• He served as the **captain** of the Indian national team during the **2016 Rio Olympics** and led the team to the silver medal at the **2016 Champions Trophy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Awards and Recognitions:**
 
 
• In **2021**, Sreejesh was honored with the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award**, which is the highest sporting honor in **India**.
 
• He was awarded the **Padma Shri**, India's fourth-highest civilian award, in **2017** for his contributions to sports.
 
• He was named the **World Games Athlete of the Year** for **2021**, becoming only the second Indian after Rani Rampal to achieve this feat.
 
• Sreejesh won the **FIH Goalkeeper of the Year** award for two consecutive years in **2021** and **2022**.
 
 
 
• **Major Achievements:**
 
 
• He won the **Gold Medal** at the **2014 Incheon Asian Games** and the **2022 Hangzhou Asian Games**.
 
• He was part of the team that secured the **Gold Medal** at the **2011, 2016, 2018, and 2023 Asian Champions Trophy**.
 
• Following his retirement, he was appointed as the **Head Coach** of the **India U-21 Men's Hockey Team** to nurture future talent.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Personal Background:** Born on **May 8, 1988**, in **Kizhakkambalam, Kerala**, Sreejesh is often referred to as **"The Wall of Indian Hockey"** due to his exceptional goalkeeping skills.
 
• **Historic Save:** His most iconic moment came during the **Tokyo 2020 Olympics** bronze medal match against **Germany**, where he made a crucial save from a penalty corner in the final **6.8 seconds** to secure the **5-4 win**.
 
• **Transition to Coaching:** His retirement marks the end of an era, but his transition to coaching ensures his vast experience in **international hockey** continues to benefit **Hockey India** and the development of junior goalkeepers.
 
• **Legacy:** He is widely regarded as one of the greatest goalkeepers in the history of the sport, alongside legends like **Shankar Lakshman**.
</ul

questions.question: What is India's rank in the Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) 2026?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**23rd**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the latest data provided, **India** has secured the **23rd** position in the **Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) 2026**.
 
• The **CCPI** is an independent monitoring tool that tracks the climate protection performance of **63 countries** and the **European Union**, which collectively account for over **90%** of global **greenhouse gas emissions**.
 
• The index is published annually by **Germanwatch**, the **NewClimate Institute**, and the **Climate Action Network (CAN) International** to enhance transparency in international climate politics.
 
• The rankings are determined by a standardized framework that allows for a comparison of climate protection efforts across different nations.
 
• The **CCPI 2026** assessment highlights how countries are aligning their national strategies with the goals set under the **Paris Agreement** to limit global warming.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Four Pillars of CCPI:** The index evaluates performance based on four categories with specific weightages: **Greenhouse Gas Emissions** (**40%**), **Renewable Energy** (**20%**), **Energy Use** (**20%**), and **Climate Policy** (**20%**).
 
• **Empty Top Three Ranks:** A unique feature of the **CCPI** is that the **first three ranks** are typically left vacant. This is because no single country has yet performed well enough in all categories to be on a path compatible with the **1.5°C** goal of the **Paris Agreement**.
 
• **Publication History:** The **Climate Change Performance Index** was first published in **2005**. It serves as a vital resource for non-governmental organizations and policymakers to pressure governments for more ambitious climate action.
 
• **India's Climate Trajectory:** India has historically performed well in the **Renewable Energy** and **GHG Emissions** categories due to its low per capita emissions and massive scale-up of solar and wind power projects.
 
• **Methodology:** The **Climate Policy** category is evaluated based on expert assessments from local NGOs and think tanks within each country, ensuring a mix of quantitative data and qualitative policy review.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **23rd** rank indicates a shift in the global competitive landscape of climate action, emphasizing the need for **India** to further accelerate its transition toward a **Net Zero** economy by its target year of **2070**.
 
• Significant contributors to a country's score include its **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)** and the implementation of domestic laws like the **Energy Conservation Act** in the context of **India**.
 
• The index often features **Nordic** countries like **Denmark** and **Sweden** near the top of the list, serving as benchmarks for climate policy and renewable integration.

questions.question: 'Strengthening Global South Cooperation for a More Inclusive and Sustainable Governance' was the theme of the 17th summit of which international organization held in July 2025?.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**BRICS**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **17th BRICS Summit** is scheduled to be held in **July 2025** under the **Presidency of Brazil**.
 
• The theme of the summit is **'Strengthening Global South Cooperation for a More Inclusive and Sustainable Governance'**, reflecting the group's focus on amplifying the voices of developing nations in the international arena.
 
• This summit is particularly significant as it continues the momentum of the **BRICS expansion** that took place during the **15th Summit** in **South Africa** and the **16th Summit** in **Russia**.
 
• The primary objectives of the **2025 summit** include promoting **multilateralism**, reforming **global financial institutions**, and enhancing **south-south cooperation** to address challenges like **climate change** and **economic inequality**.
 
• The **Brazilian presidency** aims to use this platform to advocate for **sustainable development** and a more equitable **global governance** system that represents the current **geopolitical realities**. ***Hence, the correct answer is BRICS.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Evolution of BRICS:**
 
 
• The acronym **BRIC** was first coined by **Jim O'Neill** of **Goldman Sachs** in **2001** to describe the fast-growing economies of **Brazil**, **Russia**, **India**, and **China**.
 
• The first formal summit took place in **Yekaterinburg, Russia**, in **2009**. With the induction of **South Africa** in **2010**, the group was renamed **BRICS**.
 
 
 
• **BRICS Expansion (BRICS+):**
 
 
• In a historic move during the **2023 Johannesburg Summit**, the group invited new members to join. As of **January 1, 2024**, nations including **Egypt**, **Ethiopia**, **Iran**, and the **United Arab Emirates (UAE)** became full members.
 
• This expansion significantly increases the group's share of the **global population** and its control over **global energy resources**, particularly **oil** and **gas**.
 
 
 
• **Key Institutions:**
 
 
• **New Development Bank (NDB):** Formerly known as the **BRICS Development Bank**, it is headquartered in **Shanghai, China**. It aims to mobilize resources for **infrastructure** and **sustainable development projects** in **BRICS** and other **emerging economies**.
 
• **Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA):** A framework designed to provide protection against **global liquidity pressures** and provide **mutual support** during **financial crises**.
 
 
 
• **Global Economic Impact:**
 
 
• The **BRICS** nations combined represent over **40%** of the **world's population** and contribute more than **30%** of the **global Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** based on **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)**.
 
• The group serves as a counterweight to the **G7** and seeks to challenge the dominance of the **US Dollar** in **international trade** through initiatives like **local currency settlements**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: The Quality Council of India (QCI), the national custodian of accreditation in India, commemorated the World Accreditation Day, 2025, in which city?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**New Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Quality Council of India (QCI)**, acting as the national custodian of accreditation in India, commemorated **World Accreditation Day 2025** in **New Delhi**.
 
• **World Accreditation Day** is a global initiative established by the **International Laboratory Accreditation Cooperation (ILAC)** and the **International Accreditation Forum (IAF)** to raise awareness about the importance of accreditation.
 
• The event, held on **June 9, 2025**, brought together various stakeholders, including government officials, industry leaders, and accreditation bodies, to discuss the role of quality standards in national development.
 
• The celebration in **New Delhi** focused on how accreditation supports the implementation of **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** and enhances the global competitiveness of Indian products and services.
 
• As the apex body for quality, **QCI** utilizes this platform to strengthen the quality ecosystem in India under the **Ministry of Commerce and Industry**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Quality Council of India (QCI):**
 
 
• It was established in **1997** as an autonomous body through a **Cabinet decision**.
 
• It was set up jointly by the **Government of India** and the Indian industry represented by three premier industry associations: **ASSOCHAM**, **CII**, and **FICCI**.
 
• The **Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)**, under the **Ministry of Commerce and Industry**, is the nodal department for **QCI**.
 
• The **Chairperson** of **QCI** is appointed by the **Prime Minister of India** based on the recommendation of the industry. **Jaxay Shah** was appointed to this position in **October 2022**.
 
 
 
• **Constituent Boards of QCI:**
 
 
• **NABL:** National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories, which provides accreditation to laboratories.
 
• **NABH:** National Accreditation Board for Hospitals & Healthcare Providers, focusing on quality standards in the healthcare sector.
 
• **NABET:** National Accreditation Board for Education and Training, which works on improving standards in vocational and school education.
 
• **NABCB:** National Accreditation Board for Certification Bodies, which accredits organizations offering certification and inspection services.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Accreditation:** It provides a formal recognition that an organization is competent to perform specific tasks, thereby reducing risk and increasing **consumer confidence**.
 
• **Global Context:** India is a signatory to the **ILAC Mutual Recognition Arrangement (MRA)** and **IAF Multilateral Recognition Arrangement (MLA)**, ensuring that Indian accreditations are recognized in over **100 countries**.
 
• **Economic Impact:** By adhering to international quality standards, Indian exporters can overcome **Technical Barriers to Trade (TBT)**, facilitating smoother entry into **international markets**.
 
• **World Accreditation Day History:** The first World Accreditation Day was celebrated in **2008**, and since then, it has been observed annually on **June 9** with a unique theme each year focusing on different aspects of quality and trade.
</ul

questions.question: Which award highlights lifetime achievement in sports broadcasting, won by David Hill in 2025?

options.text: Sports Business Journal's Lifetime Achievement Award
Sports Business Journal' Laureus Media Honour

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sports Business Journal's Lifetime Achievement Award**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **David Hill**, the legendary television executive and former leader of **Fox Sports**, has been selected as the recipient of the **Sports Business Journal’s Lifetime Achievement Award** for **2025**.
 
• This prestigious award recognizes individuals who have made a significant and enduring impact on the **sports business** landscape through **innovation**, **leadership**, and **visionary** contributions.
 
• The ceremony to honor **Hill** is scheduled to take place during the **18th annual Sports Business Awards** on **May 21, 2025**, in **New York City**.
 
• **David Hill** is widely celebrated for revolutionizing **sports broadcasting**, most notably by introducing the **constant score and clock graphic** (known as the **Fox Box**) during **NFL** and **MLB** broadcasts.
 
• Throughout his career, he has been a transformative figure at **News Corp**, **Sky Sports**, and **Fox**, fundamentally changing how fans across the **United States** and the **United Kingdom** consume live sports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sports Business Journal (SBJ):** 
 
 
• It is a leading **national weekly trade publication** that provides comprehensive coverage of the **sports industry**, including **marketing**, **media**, and **facility development**.
 
• The **Lifetime Achievement Award** is one of its highest honors, previously awarded to icons such as **Billie Jean King**, **Jerry Jones**, and **Dick Ebersol**.
 
 
 
• **Career of David Hill:**
 
 
• Born in **Australia**, **Hill** began his career in **journalism** before moving into **television production**.
 
• In the **1990s**, he moved to the **United States** to help launch **Fox Sports** after the network famously outbid **CBS** for the **NFL's NFC package** in **1994**.
 
• He served as the **Chairman and CEO** of **Fox Sports** and later as the **President** of **Fox Sports Media Group**, overseeing major events like the **Super Bowl**, **World Series**, and **Daytona 500**.
 
 
 
• **Technical Innovations:**
 
 
• Beyond the **Fox Box**, **Hill** was instrumental in developing the **FoxTrax** (the "glowing puck") for the **NHL** and enhancing the **audio quality** of **NASCAR** broadcasts to make viewers feel closer to the action.
 
• His work emphasized the **entertainment** aspect of sports, integrating **music**, **dynamic graphics**, and **innovative camera angles**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Influence:** Before his success in **America**, **David Hill** played a critical role in the **1991** launch of **Sky Sports** in the **United Kingdom**, which transformed the **English Premier League** into a global media powerhouse.
 
• **Industry Impact:** The **2025** award highlights his ability to blend **technology** with **storytelling**, a legacy that continues to influence every major **sports network** today, including **ESPN**, **NBC**, and **Turner Sports**.
 
• **Recognition:** In addition to the **SBJ** honor, **Hill** has won multiple **Sports Emmy Awards** and is a member of the **Sports Broadcasting Hall of Fame** (inducted in **2017**).

questions.question: Which organisation is set to be established at GIFT City, Gandhinagar from the beginning of 2026 to strengthen India’s artificial intelligence ecosystem through collaboration between government, industry, and academia?

options.text: Centre for Advanced Artificial Intelligence Research

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian AI Research Organization**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian AI Research Organization** (often referred to in the context of the **IndiaAI Innovation Centre**) is a pivotal institution designed to be the cornerstone of India’s technological advancement in the field of **Artificial Intelligence**.
 
• This organization is scheduled to be established at **GIFT City (Gujarat International Finance Tec-City)** in **Gandhinagar**, with operations expected to commence from the **beginning of 2026**.
 
• The primary mandate of the organization is to strengthen the domestic **AI ecosystem** by facilitating high-level collaboration between **government bodies**, **private industry players**, and **academic institutions**.
 
• It functions as a central part of the **IndiaAI Mission**, aiming to develop indigenous **Foundational Models** and **Large Language Models (LLMs)** tailored to the Indian context and languages.
 
• The establishment aims to reduce India's dependence on foreign AI technologies by fostering **Research and Development (R&D)** and creating a robust pipeline for **AI talent** and **intellectual property**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The IndiaAI Mission:** Approved by the **Union Cabinet** in **March 2024**, the mission has a total financial outlay of **Rs. 10,372.92 crore**. It is implemented by the **IndiaAI Independent Business Division (IBD)** under the **Digital India Corporation**.
 
• **Computing Infrastructure:** A significant portion of the mission involves the **IndiaAI Supercomputing Capacity**, which aims to establish a high-end scalable AI computing ecosystem with **10,000 or more GPUs** (Graphics Processing Units) through public-private partnerships.
 
• **GIFT City, Gandhinagar:** As India's first **International Financial Services Centre (IFSC)** and a dedicated **Smart City**, it provides a regulatory-friendly environment and world-class infrastructure, making it an ideal **location** for global tech hubs and research organizations.
 
• **IndiaAI Datasets Platform:** This initiative under the mission will provide **non-personal datasets** to Indian startups and researchers, ensuring they have the high-quality data necessary to train complex **AI models**.
 
• **Socio-Economic Applications:** The research conducted will focus on critical sectors such as **Healthcare**, **Agriculture**, and **Education**, utilizing **AI** to solve large-scale problems specific to the Indian population and geography.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ministry Involvement:** The initiative is spearheaded by the **Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)** to ensure India remains competitive in the global **AI race**.
 
• **Startup Support:** The **IndiaAI Startup Financing** pillar is designed to provide streamlined funding and support for **deep-tech startups**, enabling them to move from prototypes to commercial products.
 
• **Future Skills:** The mission includes **IndiaAI FutureSkills**, which focuses on increasing the availability of **AI courses** at undergraduate, graduate, and post-graduate levels to build a workforce of **AI professionals**.
 
• **Data Governance:** The framework emphasizes ethical **AI development** and **data privacy**, aligning with India's broader digital governance goals and the **Digital Personal Data Protection Act**.

questions.question: What is the estimated capital expenditure allocation for FY2025–26?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹11.21 lakh crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of India**, under the leadership of Union Finance Minister **Nirmala Sitharaman**, has significantly increased the outlay for **Capital Expenditure** (CapEx) to drive economic growth.
 
• For the upcoming fiscal cycle, the estimated capital expenditure allocation has been set at **₹11.21 lakh crore**, which is a substantial rise intended to modernize **infrastructure** across the nation.
 
• This allocation reflects the government's commitment to the "**Viksit Bharat**" vision, focusing on long-term asset creation rather than short-term consumption.
 
• The **₹11.21 lakh crore** figure represents approximately **3.4%** of the **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**, indicating a massive push towards capital-intensive projects.

questions.question: What is the name of India’s first 5.5 Gen stealth aircraft showcased by DRDO at Aero India 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA)** is India’s indigenous program to develop a **5.5 Generation** stealth multi-role fighter aircraft.
 
• During **Aero India 2025**, held at **Air Force Station Yelahanka** in **Bengaluru**, the **DRDO** (Defence Research and Development Organisation) showcased the progress and the stealth features of the **AMCA**.
 
• The project is spearheaded by the **Aeronautical Development Agency (ADA)** in collaboration with **Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL)**.
 
• It is designed to possess **stealth characteristics**, including a low **Radar Cross-Section (RCS)**, achieved through a special airframe design, **internal weapons bays**, and the use of **Radar Absorbent Materials (RAM)**.
 
• The **AMCA** is intended to be a **twin-engine** aircraft capable of **supercruise** (supersonic flight without using afterburners) and equipped with advanced **AESA radar** and integrated avionics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **LCA Tejas Mk-2**: 
 
 
• This is a **4.5-generation** medium-weight fighter currently under development to replace the **Mirage 2000**, **Jaguar**, and **MiG-29** fleets of the **Indian Air Force**.
 
• It features a more powerful **GE-F414** engine compared to the Mk-1 and has a higher payload capacity.
 
 
 
• **TEDBF (Twin Engine Deck Based Fighter)**: 
 
 
• This is a carrier-based multi-role combat aircraft being developed for the **Indian Navy**.
 
• It is intended to operate from India's indigenous aircraft carrier, **INS Vikrant**, and the **INS Vikramaditya**, replacing the **MiG-29K**.
 
 
 
• **Advanced Light Weight Torpedo (ALWT)**: 
 
 
• This refers to naval ammunition rather than an aircraft; it is an anti-submarine weapon developed by **NSTL** (Naval Science and Technological Laboratory) under **DRDO**.
 
 
 
• **Stealth Technology**: 
 
 
• Stealth technology involves techniques used to make aircraft, ships, or missiles less visible to **radar**, **infrared**, and **sonar** detection. 
 
• The **AMCA** incorporates a **"serpentine" intake duct** to shield the engine fan blades, which are a major source of radar reflection.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Phased Development**: The **AMCA** is planned to be developed in two phases: **Mark-1** (equipped with US-made **GE-414** engines) and **Mark-2** (which aims to use a more powerful **indigenous engine** currently being planned in collaboration with international partners).
 
• **Aero India 2025**: This is the **15th edition** of the biennial air show, serving as a major hub for the **"Make in India"** initiative in the defense and aerospace sectors.
 
• **Operational Timeline**: The first prototype of the **AMCA** is expected to be rolled out by **2028-2029**, with flight testing commencing shortly after.
 
• **Strategic Significance**: With the successful induction of **AMCA**, India will join a select group of nations, including the **USA (F-22, F-35)**, **Russia (Su-57)**, and **China (J-20)**, that possess indigenous fifth-generation stealth fighter technology.

questions.question: Launched in March 2024 in India, what is the name of the platform that allows individuals to report fraudulent communications, including calls, texts, and WhatsApp messages?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chakshu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Government of India launched the **Chakshu** facility on **March 4, 2024**, as a significant step towards enhancing **citizen security** in the telecommunications sector.
 
• **Chakshu** is an integrated feature of the **Sanchar Saathi** portal (sancharsaathi.gov.in), developed by the **Department of Telecommunications (DoT)**.
 
• The platform allows citizens to proactively report suspected **fraudulent communications** received through **calls**, **SMS**, or social media platforms like **WhatsApp**. ***Hence, the statement regarding its function is correct.***
 
• It specifically targets reporting for scams related to **KYC updates**, **bank account** or **SIM card** deactivation threats, **gas connection** issues, and **impersonation** of government officials or relatives.
 
• The initiative aims to create a **secure digital ecosystem** by allowing the **DoT** to identify and block mobile numbers and resources used by **cyber-criminals** before they can cause financial harm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Digital Intelligence Platform (DIP):** 
 
 
• Alongside **Chakshu**, the **Union Minister for Communications, Ashwini Vaishnaw**, launched the **Digital Intelligence Platform (DIP)**.
 
• The **DIP** is a non-public portal designed for **real-time information sharing** and coordination among **Telecom Service Providers (TSPs)**, **Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs)**, and **Financial Institutions**.
 
• It helps in identifying the **misuse of telecom resources** and aids in the investigation of **cyber-crimes** and **financial frauds**.
 
 
 
• **Sanchar Saathi Portal:**
 
 
• This is a **citizen-centric** initiative of the **Department of Telecommunications** to empower mobile subscribers.
 
• Other key features include **CEIR (Central Equipment Identity Register)** for blocking lost or stolen mobiles and **TAFCOP** to check the number of **mobile connections** taken in one's name.
 
 
 
• **Reporting Mechanism:**
 
 
• If a user has already fallen victim to a **financial fraud** or **cyber-crime**, they should not use **Chakshu**; instead, they must report it to the **cyber-crime helpline number 1930** or visit the official portal at **www.cybercrime.gov.in**.
 
• **Chakshu** is strictly for **suspected fraud** attempts rather than reported losses.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Impact of Telecom Security:** Since the inception of the **Sanchar Saathi** portal, the government has successfully disconnected over **1 crore mobile connections** obtained through **fraudulent means**.
 
• **Legal Framework:** These initiatives are backed by the **Telecommunications Act, 2023**, which provides the necessary legal teeth to handle **spam** and **fraudulent activities**.
 
• **Proactive Action:** By reporting on **Chakshu**, a user helps the **Department of Telecommunications** to trigger **re-verification** of the suspect number. If the re-verification fails, the **SIM card** is disconnected immediately.
 
• **Future Scope:** The platform is expected to evolve to include **AI-based** detection of **phishing** links and automated **spam filtering** in collaboration with **TSPs** like **Airtel**, **Jio**, and **VI**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following national parks was designated as 58th tiger reserve of India in March 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhav National Park**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **March 2025**, the Government of India officially notified **Madhav National Park** as the **58th Tiger Reserve** of the country.
 
• It is located in the **Shivpuri district** of **Madhya Pradesh** and spans an area of approximately **354 square kilometers**.
 
• The designation was finalized following the recommendation and approval of the **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)** to ensure better protection and habitat management for the big cats.
 
• This declaration makes **Madhav National Park** the **eighth tiger reserve** in the state of **Madhya Pradesh**, further strengthening its reputation as India’s **"Tiger State"**.
 
• The primary objective of this designation is to facilitate the **re-establishment** of a breeding tiger population in the **Gwalior-Chambal region**, where tigers had historically roamed but had disappeared over the decades.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Madhav National Park.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Panna National Park**:
 
 
• Located in **Panna and Chhatarpur districts** of **Madhya Pradesh**, it was declared a **Tiger Reserve** in **1994**.
 
• It is famous for its successful **Tiger Reintroduction Project** started in **2009** after the local tiger population had vanished.
 
• It is also home to the **Ken River**, which is part of the **Ken-Betwa river linking project**.
 
 
 
• **Pench National Park**:
 
 
• This park straddles the border of **Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra**. It was designated a **Tiger Reserve** in **1992**.
 
• It served as the inspiration for **Rudyard Kipling’s** famous work, **"The Jungle Book"**, featuring the character **Mowgli**.
 
• The park is named after the **Pench River** that flows through it from north to south.
 
 
 
• **Kuno National Park**:
 
 
• Located in the **Sheopur district** of **Madhya Pradesh**, it gained global attention in **September 2022**.
 
• It is the site for the **Action Plan for Introduction of Cheetah in India**, where **African Cheetahs** from **Namibia** and **South Africa** were released.
 
• While it hosts a variety of predators, it has not yet been designated as a primary **Tiger Reserve**.
 
 
 
• **Madhav National Park History**:
 
 
• Established in **1958**, it was named after **Madho Rao Scindia**, the Maharaja of Gwalior.
 
• The park features the **Sakhya Sagar Lake**, a **Ramsar site**, and the **George Castle**, built at the highest point for **King George V**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Project Tiger**: Launched on **April 1, 1973**, from **Jim Corbett National Park**, it is a major conservation program to protect the **National Animal** of India.
 
• **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)**: A statutory body constituted under the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**, responsible for the management of **Tiger Reserves**.
 
• **Conservation Status**: Tigers are listed as **Endangered** on the **IUCN Red List** and are included in **Schedule I** of the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**.
 
• **Ecological Corridor**: The **Madhav Tiger Reserve** is vital as it acts as a bridge between the **Ranthambore Tiger Reserve** in **Rajasthan** and the **Kuno-Panna** landscape, facilitating the natural dispersal of **wildlife**.
 
• **Tiger Census**: India conducts a **National Tiger Estimation** every **four years**. According to recent reports, India holds more than **75%** of the world's **wild tiger population**.

questions.question: Who set a javelin F42 world record (61.17 m) at the 2025 WPA Grand Prix?

• He recorded a monumental throw of **61.17 meters**, surpassing previous benchmarks in the **F42 classification**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Gurjar Mahendra.***
 
• The **F42 category** is designated for para-athletes with **lower limb impairments**, such as leg length differences or impaired muscle power, which affects their movement but allows them to compete from a standing position.
 
• **Mahendra's** achievement is a significant milestone for **Indian para-sports**, showcasing the high level of technical skill and physical preparation among Indian field athletes.

• **Para-Athletics Classifications (Javelin):**
 
 
• **F42:** This class is for athletes with a **single leg impairment** above the knee or a combination of limb deficiencies that result in similar functional limitations.

questions.question: Operation Alert, launched by the Border Security Force in August 2025, primarily aimed to strengthen security along which Indian border?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Operation Alert** was officially launched by the **Border Security Force (BSF)** in **August 2025** to enhance security and vigilance along the **International Border (IB)** between **India** and **Pakistan**.
 
• The primary focus of this intensive security exercise was the **Rajasthan border**, which includes critical sectors such as **Jaisalmer**, **Barmer**, **Bikaner**, and **Sri Ganganagar**.
 
• This operation is traditionally carried out in the days leading up to **Independence Day** on **15 August** to prevent any attempts of **infiltration**, **smuggling**, or anti-national activities by **terrorist** elements during the national festival.
 
• During **Operation Alert**, the **BSF** increases its manpower on the frontline, deploying even those personnel usually assigned to administrative tasks to ensure **24/7** surveillance and patrolling.
 
• The operation involves advanced **electronic surveillance**, increased camel patrolling in the **Thar Desert**, and coordination with local police and intelligence agencies to maintain a high state of readiness.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Border Security Force (BSF):**
 
 
• The **BSF** was established on **1 December 1965** following the **Indo-Pak War** to ensure the security of the borders of **India**.
 
• It is one of the five **Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF)** and is under the administrative control of the **Ministry of Home Affairs**.
 
• The **BSF** is currently responsible for guarding the **3,323 km** long **India-Pakistan** border and the **4,096 km** long **India-Bangladesh** border.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Context of Rajasthan Border:**
 
 
• The **International Border** in **Rajasthan** spans approximately **1,037 km**.
 
• The terrain is characterized by shifting sand dunes of the **Thar Desert**, making it a challenging environment for surveillance, requiring specialized units like the **BSF Camel Contingent**.
 
 
 
• **Related Operations:**
 
 
• Apart from **Operation Alert**, the **BSF** conducts **Operation Sard Hawa** during the winter months (usually **January**) to counter infiltration during periods of thick fog along the **western border**.
 
• These exercises are crucial for testing the operational efficiency of **surveillance equipment** and the physical readiness of the **jawans** in extreme weather conditions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Strategic Importance:** The **Rajasthan border** is strategically sensitive due to its proximity to **Pakistan's** Sindh and Punjab provinces.
 
• **Technology Integration:** Under the **Comprehensive Integrated Border Management System (CIBMS)**, the **BSF** utilizes **drones**, **thermal imagers**, and **underground sensors** to monitor the **Rajasthan** frontier.
 
• **Public Safety:** Such operations also aim to boost the confidence of the **civilian population** living in the border villages by showcasing the strength and presence of the **armed forces**.
</ul

• The project involved bringing cheetahs from **Namibia** (8 cheetahs) and **South Africa** (12 cheetahs) to restore the species in India after it was declared extinct in the country in **1952**.
 
• **Kuno National Park** is located in the **Sheopur** and **Morena** districts of **Madhya Pradesh**. It was selected because of its suitable **grassland-woodland** habitat and adequate prey base.
 
• The birth of cubs to an **India-born** mother is considered a critical indicator of the long-term success of the reintroduction program, proving that the translocated population can successfully mature and reproduce in the local environment.

• **Gir National Park:**
 
 
• Located in **Gujarat**, it is the only natural habitat in the world where **Asiatic Lions** are found.
 
• It was established in **1965** and plays a vital role in the conservation of the **Panthera leo leo** subspecies.
 
 
 
• **Ranthambore National Park:**
 
 
• Situated in the **Sawai Madhopur** district of **Rajasthan**, it is one of the most famous **Tiger Reserves** in India.
 
• It is located at the junction of the **Aravalli** and **Vindhya** hill ranges and is known for its diurnal **Bengal Tigers**.
 
 
 
• **Bandipur National Park:**
 
 
• Located in the state of **Karnataka**, it was established as a tiger reserve under **Project Tiger** in **1973**.
 
• It is a part of the **Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve** and is known for its significant population of **Elephants** and **Tigers**.
 
 
 
• **Cheetah Extinction in India:**
 
 
• The cheetah was officially declared **extinct** from India in **1952** due to over-hunting and habitat loss.
 
• The last physical evidence of the Asiatic cheetah in India was recorded in **1947** in the **Korea** district of present-day **Chhattisgarh**.

• **Geographical Features of Kuno:** The park spans an area of approximately **748 square kilometers**. It is characterized by **Kardhai**, **Khair**, and **Salai** trees and is intersected by the **Kuno River**, which is a major tributary of the **Chambal River**.
 
• **Monitoring and Management:** The cheetahs in **Kuno** are monitored 24/7 using **satellite radio collars** and dedicated ground teams to ensure their safety and health within the **acclimatization bomas** and the open forest.
 
• **Species Difference:** The cheetahs introduced in Kuno are **African Cheetahs** (Acinonyx jubatus jubatus), as the **Asiatic Cheetah** population is currently restricted only to **Iran** and is too small to permit translocation.
